claims.text: The starting cast CoCrFeNi-based or TiZrNb-based alloy has limited ductility, grains larger than 10 μm, and is prone to brittle intermetallic formation during cooling.
Combined addition of 0.5–1.5 at.% C and 1.0–3.0 at.% O can produce a massive interstitial solid solution without carbide or oxide precipitation.
High-energy ball milling or high-pressure torsion will refine the alloy to grain sizes below 50 nm.
Annealing at 900 °C for 3 min or 500 °C for 2 h can stabilize the nanocrystalline structure without carbide or oxide precipitation.
A deformation-generated dislocation density above 10^15 m^-2 is required for the proposed processing route.
Oxygen forms Ordered Oxygen Complexes in Ti/Zr-rich or Co/Cr-rich chemical short-range-order regions.
Carbon addition stabilizes an FCC phase against transformation to HCP in CoCrFeNi-based alloys.
Carbon increases stacking-fault energy in the proposed alloys.
Ordered Oxygen Complexes act as dislocation-pinning centers.
Ordered Oxygen Complexes promote cross-slip and wavy slip, thereby enhancing ductility.
Carbon-induced stacking-fault-energy modulation promotes nanotwinning and enables TWIP/TRIP behavior.
Grain-boundary segregation of C and N lowers interfacial energy and prevents grain coarsening during annealing.
The combined route will retain a dual-phase FCC+BCC or FCC+HCP solid-solution structure with grain size below 50 nm.
The processed alloy will have yield strength above 800 MPa and elongation above 20%.
The processed alloy will contain no detectable brittle Laves or M23C6 phases.
The cast or conventionally annealed baseline has grains above 1 μm, yield strength below 400 MPa, and elongation below 10%.
Oxygen contents above 3.0 at.% cause grain-boundary segregation and brittle fracture.
Exceeding the carbon or alloying-element solid-solution limit causes carbide precipitation, including M23C6 or Mo4C.
Annealing beyond a critical time window causes grain coarsening or intermetallic nucleation.
Massive interstitial content produces extreme lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening.

contradictions.description: The target explicitly includes FCC+HCP or FCC+BCC dual phases, but the mechanism says carbon suppresses transformation into HCP/BCC and labels those structures as brittle phases or intermetallics.
The grain-boundary stabilization mechanism invokes segregation of C and N, but nitrogen is not included in the proposed alloying intervention.
The boundary predicts brittle fracture above 3 at.% O as the expected instability limit, whereas the falsification rule says observing that same predicted behavior would falsify the hypothesis.
Carbon is said both to increase stacking-fault energy and to promote nanotwinning/TWIP/TRIP, but no explanation is given for how the proposed increase preserves the low-SFE deformation modes.
